title: My R Palmer Penguin Analysis
text:
I’m investigating how flipper length varies among penguin species and between sexes.
Data: Palmer Penguins, Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.

library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)


penguins_cleaned <- penguins |>
    drop_na(species, sex, bill_length_mm, flipper_length_mm) |>
    group_by(species, sex)


penguins_summarised <- penguins_cleaned   |>
    summarise(mean_flipper_len = mean(flipper_length_mm),
             mean_bill_len = mean(bill_length_mm))


ggplot(
  penguins_cleaned,
  aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm, fill = sex)
) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    x = "Species",
    y = "Flipper length (mm)",
    fill = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()







Figure 1: Flipper length by penguin species and sex.

What I found
The data shows that males have longer flipper lengths than the female of their speieces and that flipper length between species differs. With the boxplot we can clearly see the differences of the Gentoo penguins who have the longer flipper lengths than the other two species Adeille and Chinstrap.

title: My First Weeks in MDS
text:
First Week in MDS
Orientation
Orientation for MDS was a whirlwind of emotions. Lots of excitements and eager to meet my new classmates but also anxious about what the next 10 months will be like. The first day was a lot of information to take in but on the next day the scavenger hunt was a great way to explore the campus and get to know some classmates.
First Week of Class
First weeks of classes was tougher than I thought it would be but I also learned how to use the terminal which was really fun. I also did not expect the assignments to take as long as they did. What surprised me the most was how quickly I got used to being a student working full time right up to the start of orientation.
Current Thoughts
In week 2, I mostly think about what the next week will be like and try to finish my assignments soon so I have enough time to study as well.

title: My Python Palmer Penguin Analysis
text:
I am investigating how flipper length varies among penguin species and between sexes, but this time I am doing this on python!
Data: Palmer Penguins, Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins


penguins = load_penguins()

penguins_cleaned = (
    penguins
    .dropna(subset=[
        "species",
        "sex",
        "bill_length_mm",
        "flipper_length_mm"
    ])
)


penguins_summarised = (
    penguins_cleaned
    .groupby(["species", "sex"])
    .agg(
        mean_flipper_len=("flipper_length_mm", "mean"),
        mean_bill_len=("bill_length_mm", "mean")
    )
    .reset_index()
)


sns.boxplot(
data=penguins_cleaned,
x="species",
y="flipper_length_mm",
hue="sex",
palette=["#FF1493","#C8A2C8"],
order=["Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo"]
)

plt.xlabel("Species")
plt.ylabel("Flipper length (mm)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Flipper length by penguin species and sex.

title: About
text:
Why Data Science
My background in health sciences sparked my interest in the power of data and the insights it can provide. While I am particularly interested in applying data science to healthcare initiatives, planning and decision-making, I am also excited by its potential across a variety of industries. Through data science, I enjoy uncovering patterns, answering meaningful questions and discovering the stories that data can tell. I hope to use these skills to support data-driven solutions that create a positive impact.

Outside of Data Science
Outside of data science, you can usually find me with a book. I enjoy reading, staying active and spending quality time with friends and family. I also love to bake and decorate cakes.
